page: Microsoft Azure EC16eds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance driven by an Intel x86_64 processor executing on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is provisioned with 16 dedicated vCPUs and 128.0 GB of memory, delivering an 8.0 GB per vCPU allocation ratio. Graphical processing units are not integrated into this configuration.

Storage capability on the EC16eds_v6 includes 945 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD capacity in addition to compatibility with Azure Premium Storage remote disks. The direct-attached NVMe storage acts as fast ephemeral space for temporary databases, swap files, and operational caching layers. The instance does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Resource allocation efficiency stems from the dense 1:8 compute-to-memory relationship, which suits workloads that encounter memory bottlenecks before processing limits. The provision of 945 GB of local NVMe SSD eliminates the need to attach external block volumes solely for scratch operations, though workloads with no requirement for temporary local disks may experience unutilized hardware capacity.

The hardware configuration supports memory-constrained workloads, including relational database management systems, in-memory caches, distributed analytics nodes, and high-throughput data extraction and transformation pipelines.

Its 1:8 compute-to-memory balance accommodates applications where memory capacity dictates instance sizing. The integrated local NVMe SSD delivers low-latency scratch space for file caching and ephemeral databases without necessitating supplementary remote block attachments. This architecture is designed for memory-intensive enterprise tasks, relational databases, in-memory caching solutions, and data analytics pipelines requiring significant RAM alongside responsive local temporary storage.
